body:
There must be one integer type. Main's `purrdf_xsd::bigint::BigInt` (base 1e9, from the exact numeric tower) and the binary integer the geodesy work built (`crate::integer::Int` on branch `paudley/408-geo-deterministic-geodesic-distance-in`: three limbs inline, allocation-free scratch variants) cannot coexist. Two integer types on main is not acceptable.

Replace main's base-1e9 representation with the binary integer:
- Extract the binary integer from the geodesy branch, with its zero-allocation guarantees and tests, as the workspace's only arbitrary-precision integer.
- Rebuild the exact tower's arithmetic on it: add, sub, mul (schoolbook and Karatsuba), div/rem, gcd, pow, sqrt_floor, mul_div_rem. Rebuild Integer, Decimal and Rational, and decimal parsing and printing, at the edges.
- Replace the base-1e9 cost model (`exact/cost.rs`, `limb_len`, `leading_u64`, `decimal_digits`) with binary-limb charges. Publish them as governor profile v14, with the vectors and corpus regenerated by their generators.
- Preserve everything: exact results on every surface (Rust, CLI, Python, C, wasm32, byte-identical natively and on wasm32), DivisionPolicy semantics, F&O error codes, determinism across thread counts, no over-refusal at the minimum answering ceilings, and the existing exact-tower tests, including the 100,000-row SUM/AVG oracle.
- Benches: small values must not regress against main, and large values must not regress against main's Karatsuba. Report both.

The geodesy PR (#463) then merges on top, sharing this integer, as governor profile v15. Refs #443, #423, #408.
title: xsd: one binary arbitrary-precision integer for the whole workspace
